newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers want trimmer USDA field offices-Glickman.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers want trimmer USDA field offices-Glickman.

text.p: Farm-state leaders in Congress want to see a more efficient network of local Agriculture Department offices, Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday.

"They have charged us to reduce our costs and duplication out there," Glickman told reporters when asked about a three-hour "summit" Monday that included congressional leaders and administration budget officers.

Senate Agriculture Committee chairman Richard Lugar, Indiana Republican, said there was a great deal of discussion of the Farm Service Agency and its workload. Lugar spearheaded reorganization of USDA earlier this decade.
"The budget...will demand efficiencies occur at the local level," Lugar told reporters.

In its fiscal 1998 budget proposal, the administration raised the possibility of closing an additional 500 local USDA offices. Downsizing originally was expected to reduce the total to 2,500. Glickman has said he would not act on closings without consulting Congress.
Glickman said there would be no immediate specific changes in operations as a result of Monday's summit.
He said lawmakers preferred streamlining and elimination of needless spending rather than merger of agencies.
